derivation: Measured 8 operating sites totalling 6.271 km² of surface, with 17.58 km of combined boundary. These figures come from mapped geometry, so each one can be opened and checked.

Substituting for contracted crews at 0.5 to 2 crew-days per manual pass, that displaces 16 to 480 contracted crew-days per month — the hours currently spent putting people on module strings, tracker rows, inverter skids and combiner boxes; array blocks and thermal hotspots.

Phase one does not require full coverage. dimensions.label: Multi-site distribution
dimensions.rationale: Number of discrete operating sites. Distributed operations multiply travel cost for contracted crews, which is exactly the cost autonomous inspection removes.

dimensions.label: Measured site footprint
dimensions.rationale: Total square kilometres of operating surface we could measure from mapped geometry. Footprint is the unit of inspection work, so it is the closest proxy for deal size.

dimensions.label: Regulated hazard exposure
dimensions.rationale: Whether the operator sits under a named inspection mandate and has disclosed safety exposure. Regulation converts inspection from discretionary to obligatory.

dimensions.label: Continuous operations
dimensions.rationale: Evidence the site runs around the clock, which makes inspection windows scarce and manual coverage expensive.

dimensions.label: Reachability
dimensions.rationale: Whether we found real named people at the target seniority with a citable source. Unreachable accounts are deprioritised, not invented into existence.

dimensions.label: Commodity & extraction match
dimensions.rationale: Does the operator extract the same commodity classes as the reference account, using comparable surface methods?

dimensions.label: Contractor dependency
dimensions.rationale: How heavily the operator's own primary filing leans on contractors, measured by verbatim mention counts in its risk factors. This is the incumbent cost being displaced.

dimensions.label: Automation readiness
dimensions.rationale: Signals of digital or automation investment. Some readiness shortens the sale; a fully solved autonomy programme removes the opportunity.

dimensions.label: Capital capacity
dimensions.rationale: Ability to fund a programme, inferred from public-market listing status and disclosed scale.

dimensions.label: Timing trigger
dimensions.rationale: A dated, cited event that makes contact relevant now — leadership change, incident, regulatory action, or expansion.

objections.objection: We already fly drones. We have a team and a pilot.

Ask what their pilot-to-aircraft ratio is; the reference deployment runs one-to-many under a regulator-approved waiver, which is the step manual programmes cannot take.

objections.objection: Our contractors are cheaper than a capital programme.

Then ask what a single contractor safety incident costs them, because their own filing already names that as a production risk and refers to contractors 15 times.

objections.objection: Our site has connectivity and power constraints in the pit.

It also sets up the honest version of our sizing, which is a range precisely because placement depends on their terrain.

discoveryQuestions.question: Who physically walks Complejo Solar Cerro Dominador today, how often, and is that your crew or a contracted one?
discoveryQuestions.whyItLands: Opens on their own ground rather than our product. We already know the feature covers 14.42 km² with 15.4 km of boundary, so the answer is checkable and the question cannot be brushed off with a generality.

discoveryQuestions.question: When an inspection finding needs to be produced for the regulator, how long does it take to assemble, and how confident are you in the timestamp on it?
discoveryQuestions.whyItLands: Most operators can answer the first half instantly and hesitate on the second. Autonomous inspection produces a timestamped, third-party-auditable record, so this question surfaces the value that is not about labour cost.

discoveryQuestions.question: You have 2056 mapped operating areas. Does each carry its own inspection crew, or do crews travel between them?
discoveryQuestions.whyItLands: Travel between separated sites is pure overhead and is invisible on a cost line. We measured the sites as 1 spatially separate cluster(s), so we can be specific about which ones share infrastructure.

discoveryQuestions.question: If inspection frequency were not constrained by crew availability, what would you want to look at more often than you currently can?
discoveryQuestions.whyItLands: Reframes from cost reduction to capability. The reference deployment did not cut inspection — it doubled frequency at lower exposure, and this question finds the asset the operator already wishes they watched more closely.

objections.objection: We already fly drones. We have a team and a pilot.
objections.response: Most operators at this scale do, and that is usually manual sortie flying rather than a scheduled autonomous programme. The distinction that matters is whether a mission runs without a person present and whether its output lands in your systems automatically. Ask what their pilot-to-aircraft ratio is; the reference deployment runs one-to-many under a regulator-approved waiver, which is the step manual programmes cannot take.

objections.objection: Our contractors are cheaper than a capital programme.
objections.response: Compare like for like. Phase one at the reference account was a single dock on one zone for a total system investment of USD 70,000 to 80,000, with return inside a year — not a site-wide capital programme. Then ask what a single contractor safety incident costs them, because their own filing already names that as a production risk.

objections.objection: Our site has connectivity and power constraints in the pit.
objections.response: That is the normal starting condition rather than a blocker, and it is why dock placement is a survey rather than an assumption. Concede the point and use it: ask which zones have power and network today, because those are exactly where phase one goes. It also sets up the honest version of our sizing, which is a range precisely because placement depends on their terrain.

objections.objection: Aviation approval in this jurisdiction will take forever.
objections.response: Do not minimise it. The reference deployment ran under approvals obtained with a local delivery partner rather than by the operator, which is the route that works. Name the partner-led model early, because an operator who thinks they must obtain the waiver themselves will stall the deal on a task that is not theirs.

objections.objection: Send me some information and I will circulate it.
objections.response: This is the polite close, and the counter is specificity. Offer the one-page account brief for their own site, naming the measured footprint, then ask who else should see it. That converts a brush-off into a second name and multi-threads the account without pressure.
